assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opened a new observational window: the IceCube detector, a cubic-kilometre of Antarctic ice instrumented as a Cherenkov telescope, established a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and then identified first sources (TXS 0506+056 in 2017-18, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane). This is the kind of instrument-driven discovery I weight most heavily: original concept, hard calibration and background rejection, and a result that created neutrino astronomy.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions are the conception and leadership of IceCube (Halzen as spokesperson and principal scientific driver, Karle as a leading experimentalist on the detector and analysis). The credited list supports a fair two-person prize. A wider history (AMANDA, DUMAND, others such as John Learned) and the size of the collaboration mean credit allocation needs careful review, and I cannot verify from the supplied text who else should be considered.
assessment.maturity: Strong. Diffuse flux is confirmed at high significance with independent analyses and ANTARES/KM3NeT-type cross-checks emerging; source identifications are newer but multiple. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the instrument-leadership credit is cleanly separable from a roughly 300-person collaboration and from precursor experiments.
Source-population interpretation is still evolving, though the existence of the flux is solid.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on the magic-wavelength idea and then realised with strontium and ytterbium at 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, are a measurement-technology advance of the first rank. They redefine the limits of timekeeping, enable tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice concept and demonstrated the first clocks; Ye brought the clock to record accuracy and coherence. A clean two-person configuration; other contributors (for example Hall and Hansch on combs, already honoured in 2005) are separate. I am relying on my general knowledge of the history here.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independent clocks in several national labs reproduce 10^-18 performance, and international comparisons are routine. Practical redefinition of the SI second is still pending, but that is not required for scientific recognition.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier 2005 and 2012 prizes in precision spectroscopy and atom control may make some members see it as incremental.
Condensed attribution among many groups (JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST) is only partly captured by two names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a standard ruler imprinted in the galaxy distribution, detected in SDSS and 2dFGRS, and are now a cornerstone of precision cosmology and dark-energy constraints. The physics is clean and the measurement technique relies on large survey instruments and careful systematics control.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein led the SDSS LRG detection; Cole and Peacock were central to the 2dFGRS detection in the same year (2005), so the supplied names reflect both discovery teams. The theory behind BAO (Peebles, Sunyaev, Zeldovich, and others) predates the measurement, which complicates the allocation. A three-person split is plausible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent surveys (BOSS, eBOSS, WiggleZ, DESI) have confirmed it, and it is central to recent DESI dark-energy discussions.
uncertainties: Who deserves credit for the original idea versus the first detection is disputed.
Recent evidence for evolving dark energy from BAO combinations remains debated and could change how the result is framed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered the first full-sky, high-fidelity CMB maps with a differential radiometer design, fixing the age, geometry and composition of the Universe and establishing the LambdaCDM concept at percent level. A major instrument-led achievement, though CMB anisotropy has previously been recognised (2006 COBE, 2019 cosmology).
assessment.attribution: Bennett as PI, Page as an instrument and calibration leader, and Spergel as the principal cosmological interpreter provide a reasonable configuration. Other WMAP team members and the earlier COBE and ground and balloon experiments (e.g., BOOMERanG, MAXIMA) also contributed, so the allocation is not unique.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and confirmed by Planck and ground-based experiments. Possible concern is that the field has been recently recognised, lowering the novelty margin.
uncertainties: Overlap with previous cosmology prizes and with Planck/ground-based experiments.
Large collaboration makes it hard to isolate the decisive individuals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Event Horizon Telescope used VLBI at 230 GHz with a planet-sized array and atomic-clock-grade timing to image the shadow of M87* and Sgr A*. It is an impressive technique-driven result, demonstrating strong-field gravity consistent with general relativity and giving a direct view of a black-hole shadow.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the array build-out and the collaboration, and Moran contributed decisive VLBI and submillimetre interferometry work. Credit among a collaboration of hundreds, including imaging and calibration teams, is hard to allocate, and I cannot independently verify the exact roles.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: two images with independent reductions and multi-epoch M87* data, with polarisation images consistent. Interpretation tests of GR remain at modest precision.
uncertainties: Large collaboration; the credited three may not reflect the decisive imaging-algorithm contributions.
Precision of GR tests is still limited and the physics novelty beyond the image is debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays have reported evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, a new window on supermassive black-hole binaries or early-Universe physics. It stands on decades of precise radio timing, the kind of patient instrumentation and calibration work I respect.
assessment.attribution: Kramer, Manchester and McLaughlin represent the EPTA, PPTA and NANOGrav efforts respectively; the decisive credit is spread across multiple collaborations and across pulsar-timing pioneers, so a fair three-person configuration is difficult and I cannot resolve it from the list.
assessment.maturity: Not yet mature: the Hellings-Downs evidence is at roughly 3-4 sigma in several arrays, with independent arrays in general agreement but no definitive detection or source identification. Premature for this year, in my view.
uncertainties: Significance below the discovery threshold and the astrophysical origin undetermined.
Attribution across three major collaborations is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, with correlated insulators and superconductivity found in a tunable platform. This is an original and widely impactful discovery, but condensed matter is outside my own expertise, so I would defer to colleagues on detailed ranking.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle theoretically; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the experimental discovery of correlated and superconducting states. A theory-plus-experiment configuration is natural, though other twisted-graphene groups (e.g., Dean, Yacoby) and Cao as first author contribute to the story.
assessment.maturity: Quite mature in terms of reproduction across many laboratories, but the field is young (since 2018) and the nature of the superconductivity is still debated; recognition could be considered early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism not settled; timing may be premature.
Credit to early-career first authors and other groups is not captured by the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects form a major conceptual and experimental development, with HgTe and magnetic-doped films providing clear measurements of edge transport. Importance is high, though I defer to condensed-matter colleagues on the relative weighting.
assessment.attribution: Kane (theory of the quantum spin Hall effect), Molenkamp (experimental observation in HgTe) and Xue (experimental quantum anomalous Hall effect) form a coherent trio, but a compound candidate with overlapping theory credit (Bernevig, Zhang, Mele, Hasan) in B045, so allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independently confirmed across many groups for over fifteen years, and the field is well established.
uncertainties: Theory credit among Kane, Mele, Zhang, Bernevig and others is contested.
The candidate combines several effects whose parts may merit different recognition.
